The presence of antiphospholipid antibodies (APL) has been investigated as a potential risk factor for avascular necrosis of bone (AVN) in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, studies have found that incorporating an adjustment for corticosteroid use was unable to show a link between the presence of APL and the development of AVN in these patients. This suggests that while APL may be associated with AVN, their presence alone is not sufficient to explain this condition.

It's essential to note that more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between SLE and AVN, as well as the role of APL in this context. Further studies are recommended to investigate the potential benefits or risks of screening for APL in patients with SLE and to identify other risk factors for AVN.

In summary, while there may be a connection between APL and AVN in some cases, more research is required to determine whether this association holds true across all individuals with SLE.
